answer: Admission under one invite root gets dearer per entrant: first pays 5 units, locked 12 epochs, each later entrant double the previous rung. Registrars read the root signal, its entrant count, and price the next rung at 5 times 2 to that count, so renaming cannot reset it. Each rung issues one receipt bound to its payment record; trying to forge one fails the registrar hash check, and it drops to nadir weight, zero, until paid in full. One payment backs one identity. An honest entrant pays 5 once, back after the lock; ten on one root lock 5,115, and 1,000 fakes across capped roots lock 511,500.
